en: So now at this point with this course, you
learned a lot about HTMX and most
importantly,
we explored all those core features and all
those core
attributes that you can add to your HTML
elements
to use HTMX to send requests to some backend
behind the scenes and then use the responses
of those requests to replace parts of the
currently rendered page.
And you learned how to send GET and POST
requests, how to send DELETE requests, how
to only select parts of the incoming
response,
and so
on.
The question therefore now is,
how do you best continue?
And one thing I would recommend that you do
is that you explore the official
documentation in addition to all the things
you learned in this course. Course, because
whilst in this course, we of course covered
all those core
attributes and many more advanced attributes
and settings,
there are still more attributes, some pretty
niche attributes that might come in handy in

And therefore I would recommend that you at
least have a look at the various attributes
you have here, at the options you have and
what they do.
So that you can maybe use some of these
attributes in situations where you need
them,
and that you also explore some other
HTMX features that might be useful to you in
certain situations.
For example, HTMX automatically adds some
CSS classes to certain elements whilst it's
performing certain actions.
There also are other headers you could set
besides the headers we covered in this
course
if you would need to further configure
responses you're sending back from the
backend to the client that is using HTMX.
Or there might be some specific event which
you might need for the application you're
building and therefore exploring those
officially supported HTMX events might also
be a good idea.
Last but not least, HTMX also offers certain
utility methods that you can use to interact
with the DOM.
You don't need to use them. For example,
instead of setting up an event listener like
this, you can also use the addEventListener
method that's built right into JavaScript.
But still knowing about these methods can
definitely be helpful.
And therefore, in a nutshell, I do recommend
that you
do at least explore the official
documentation, that you use it as an
opportunity to dive deeper and also, of
course, to look up things about which you
did learn in this course in case you forgot
about them. And in addition, also consider
exploring the examples you find on the
official website
because these examples again allow you to
practice working with HTMX. They show you
what you can do with HTMX.
And who knows, maybe you also find an
example for a certain use case or problem
you have in your application and you
therefore can learn how to implement a
certain functionality with HTMX with help of
those examples.
And if you then use all these resources and
you maybe also revisit this course from time
to time to
keep your knowledge up to date, you're well
prepared to use HTMX no matter on which
